newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt asks Spain to help in looming EU deal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt asks Spain to help in looming EU deal.

text.p: Egypt asked Spain on Wednesday to lobby its case during talks with the European Union on a trade partnership deal and invited Madrid to play a bigger role in its fledgling economy.

Egyptian ministers and economists told the 50 Spanish business people accompanying King Juan Carlos that Egypt warmly welcomes their cash and expertise and their government's help in the trade deal, snagged on disagreements on agricultural quotas.
"We're looking to Spain to help and support Egypt's position with the European Union," Egyptian Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily told the meeting.

"The partnership agreement is now at a crucial point and the agricultural offer they have given us is not compatible. We also need Spanish help in lifting the unjust procedures taken against our textiles and our potatoes," Gueily added.

Assistant Foreign Minister Gamal Bayyoumi told Reuters last week Egypt and the EU were edging towards a final deal after the 15-nation block decided to increase its quota on agricultural imports -- the main bone of contention in the talks.

The EU has also charged Egypt with dumping its textiles. Egypt has in turn said the EU was looking for a market for its industrial goods but was unwilling to let in Egypt's farm goods, namely potatoes, rice, citrus and flowers.
Spain assured Egypt it would support its case and boost its role in the economy.

"We are and we will help Egypt with the negotiations with the EU because it is in the interest of both sides," said Alvaro Rengifo, general director of commercial policy and external investments in the Spanish ministry of economy and finance.
"We know how sensitive the issue of agriculture is, we had our problems with the EU and since we all stand to gain by opening our markets, we want to help," he told Reuters.

Spain has offered Cairo financial aid of $300 million over three years -- half in soft loans and half in commercial credits set aside to finance projects of Spanish companies. If Egypt accepts, the deal would be signed later this year, Rengifo said.
Egyptian and Spanish businesspeople discussed joint ventures and the two sides called for more trade.

Manuel Otero, head of the Spanish Confederation of Employers and Industries, said that businesses prompted the king to pay this state visit to Egypt, his first since 1977, to check out investment opportunities for themselves.
Several Spanish firms have invested in Egypt, the largest being Repsol which had put in $500 million and plans to invest another $500 million in gas, Spanish officials said.

Trade with Spain makes up just two percent of Egypt's total trade with Europe and Spanish Secretary of State for Trade, Tourism and Enterprises Jose Norniella said that his country was only the 13th largest source of Egyptian imports.
